Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The return is scheduled for Thursday, May 16, at the east service entrance of Alder Creek Middle School. The site is the district’s outdoor learning area, not a commercial vendor. The district van is expected between 2:30 and 3:00 p.m.; that is an estimated arrival window, not a confirmed appointment. The school office closes at 4:00 p.m. If the van is delayed past 3:30, Mara is supposed to call the school office before setting off from the site. don’t change that into a guaranteed arrival or imply the office can receive things after closing.

The equipment was signed out for the outdoor learning program on April 22. The original checkout sheet lists two folding field tables, twelve green plastic specimen trays, one portable water-testing kit in a gray case, and a set of eight laminated stream-site cards. The checkout sheet says the testing kit case included a probe, two sample bottles, and a short cable, but the notes do not give separate asset numbers for those pieces. The field tables have school asset stickers 4418 and 4421. The tray count is a group quantity, and the cards are recorded as one set; don’t invent individual identifiers. The equipment was checked out by Evan Ruiz, the program coordinator, and Mara’s return note says she received it from Evan on May 14. It doesn’t say whether Evan personally packed it after the program ended.

There are three packing units expected: a blue lidded tote with the specimen trays and stream-site cards, a long canvas sleeve with the two folding tables, and the gray testing-kit case. Mara’s note says the blue tote lid has a split near its back hinge, first noticed during the May 14 packing, and says “the lid still closes, but it lifts if the tote is carried by the top.” Keep that quotation as a reported note, not as a new inspection result. The sleeve has a paper tag reading “FIELD TABLES — 2”; it is a tag, not proof of the count inside. The gray case is described as latched, but the return note does not confirm the probe, bottles, or cable are all present. Do not say any item has been inspected at school yet. If receiving staff observe a crack in the gray case or damage to the probe, the kit should remain out of storage until the science department lead reviews it. That condition matters; don’t turn it into a claim that damage exists or that the lead has already reviewed anything.

The sign-out sheet records the two tables as clean and dry when issued. It has no condition notes for the trays or cards. A May 13 message from Mara says the tables were wiped down after the final session, and the stream cards were kept in the tote away from water. These are statements in the records, not a fresh condition check. The water-testing kit was used on May 10 and rinsed afterward, according to Evan’s text. The text does not mention drying the probe or replacing the sample bottles. There is no calibration record in the return packet, and nobody has asked for a new calibration during this return. The prompt should keep those points separate: a rinse was reported; drying, bottle replacement, and calibration are not confirmed. Don’t suggest that a test result or calibration status is known.

1. The equipment count should be compared against the checkout sheet, but the checklist must allow staff to record an actual count rather than assume all expected pieces arrived. For the specimen trays, record how many of the twelve are physically present. For the tables, check the two asset stickers if visible and record any sticker that cannot be read. For the cards, check for the set of eight without treating them as eight separately tracked assets. For the kit, list the probe, two sample bottles, and short cable as pieces to check individually, while making clear the notes do not provide separate asset numbers. If a piece is absent, the checklist should ask for its status or follow-up, not state where it is.

2. The paperwork in the return packet consists of the April 22 checkout sheet, Mara’s May 14 return note, Evan’s May 10 text, and Mara’s May 13 message. No signed receipt, inspection form, or calibration sheet is listed. Have the checklist record which of these four documents was actually available at handoff; don’t assume a note being mentioned means it is in the packet on Thursday. A signature line may be included for the returning person and receiving staff member, with the date and time, but it should document the handoff only. It must not be phrased as a blanket confirmation that every piece is present, undamaged, clean, or accepted.

3. The return note says the split tote lid was noticed while packing on May 14, but it doesn’t say whether the split got larger or whether the tote was carried by its top afterward. Include space to record the condition seen at the school and who observed it. If staff cannot safely carry the tote by its top, they can note that and ask for another handling method; do not state that a replacement tote is available. There is no current note about damage to the tables, trays, or cards, which means their condition is unrecorded, not that they are undamaged. The checklist should distinguish a recorded observation from an item that has not yet been checked.

4. After the count and condition checks, record where the equipment was temporarily placed, if staff know, and which person is responsible for any open follow-up. No storage room or shelf has been assigned in the notes, so leave the location blank or prompt the user to fill it in. If the labels on a returned item do not match the checkout sheet, ask the receiving staff to record the wording and contact the science department lead before changing the inventory entry; the notes do not provide an alternate label or authorize a correction. Keep unresolved questions visible, especially any missing kit component, unreadable asset sticker, or uncertainty about whether the receiving staff member was present for the whole unloading. Finish with a short handoff record for the actual date and time, names or role names as available, and any follow-up owner. Mara’s note says the blue tote lid has a split near its back hinge, first noticed during packing on May 14: “the lid still closes, but it lifts if the tote is carried by the top.” Treat this as a reported note, not a new inspection result. The sleeve has a paper tag reading “FIELD TABLES — 2”; the tag does not prove the number of tables inside. The gray case is described as latched, but the return note does not confirm whether the probe, bottles, and cable are all present. No item has yet been inspected at school. If receiving staff observe a crack in the gray case or damage to the probe, the kit must remain out of storage until the science department lead reviews it. Do not imply that damage exists or that the lead has already reviewed anything.

**Condition and maintenance records**

The checkout sheet records the tables as clean and dry when issued. It contains no condition notes for the trays or cards. In a May 13 message, Mara says the tables were wiped down after the final session and the stream cards were kept in the tote away from water. List the probe, two sample bottles, and short cable as individual pieces to check, while noting that the records give them no separate asset numbers. No signed receipt, inspection form, or calibration sheet is listed. Include a way to record which of the four documents was actually available at handoff; do not assume that a mentioned note will be in the packet on Thursday. You may include signature lines for the returning person and receiving staff member, with date and time, but these should document the handoff only. No storage room or shelf is assigned in the notes, so leave the location blank or prompt the user to fill it in.
